install: Normal upstream install: `squeez update` (downloads the latest release, checks checksums.sha256, swaps the running exe by rename, refreshes Claude Code hooks), then `squeez setup --host=<h>` for each safe host.

neverSetupHosts.opencode: overwrites the owner OpenCode plugin (overlay opencode-plugin)
neverSetupHosts.codex: re-registers Codex hooks the owner keeps OFF (overlay codex-hooks-off)
neverSetupHosts.copilot: rewrites the broken top-level registration (overlay copilot-hooks, upstream #243)
neverSetupHosts.all: bare `squeez setup` runs every host above

overlays.what: Owner OpenCode plugin: on Windows the wrapper follows the OpenCode `shell` config key, not the OS. A PowerShell shell gets powershell.exe -EncodedCommand (upstream wraps with POSIX quoting and squeez wrap runs them in bash) and WSL commands bounded by a taskkill /F /T supervisor that exits 124; a bash shell gets the POSIX form with a forward-slash quoted binary path, and WSL commands are left unwrapped so the host timeout bounds them.

upstream.covers: dual export for OpenCode 2.x (this plugin is 1.x-only)

overlays.retireWhen: A squeez release's opencode-plugin/squeez.js contains the -EncodedCommand wrapping and a bounded WSL timeout (check by marker, not by changelog). Before moving OpenCode to 2.x, merge #242's dual export into this file.

overlays.what: Register squeez's Copilot CLI hooks under settings.hooks.<Event> with forward-slash paths; squeez 1.48.10 writes top-level keys Copilot ignores, with unquoted backslash paths.
overlays.retireWhen: A squeez release writes Copilot hooks under hooks.<Event> (EventRoot::Nested) with shell_arg paths; then `squeez setup --host=copilot` moves to setupHosts.

overlays.what: Owner decision (X-74, X-119): no squeez hook registered with Codex on Windows and the context-mode Codex plugin disabled, because Codex's managed daemon starts hooks without CREATE_NO_WINDOW (one flashing window per hook).

upstream.covers: CREATE_NO_WINDOW for hooks and background subprocesses
upstream.state: merged 2026-09-29; first in 0.160.0-alpha.6; no stable release yet

overlays.retireWhen: A stable Codex release containing openai/codex#49164 is installed AND the owner decides to re-enable hooks; then run `squeez setup --host=codex` and drop this overlay.

configWhy.context_window_tokens: owner pin at 1M so squeez's context meter matches the model window
configWhy.auto_compress_md: owner policy X-28/X-98/X-119: compress-md rewrote CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md on every session start; each host's init reads its own config.ini, and setup creates new host configs with true
configWhy.configRequiredWhen: a missing config.ini is not neutral: init falls back to Config::default() (init.rs load_config_from), whose auto_compress_md is true (config.rs), so a host whose init trigger exists must have its file. The OpenCode v2 profile (XDG_CONFIG_HOME=~/.opencode-v2/config) reads ~/.opencode-v2/config/opencode/squeez/config.ini, which was absent until 2026-09-30

omoClaudeHooksOff.why: oh-my-openagent runs Claude Code PreToolUse hooks on OpenCode tool calls and applies updatedInput with output.args = {...} (packages/utils/src/replace-tool-args.ts). OpenCode executes the original args object (session/tools.ts passes { args } and never reads output.args back), so the Claude hook's wrap is dropped and the squeez plugin, which runs after OMO, edits the detached copy: commands ran raw except the ones squeez should-wrap rejects. Under OpenCode the squeez plugin is the wrapper, so squeez's Claude pretooluse.sh is excluded for OMO. OMO matches the pattern against command.split('/').pop(), which for the registered command is pretooluse.sh followed by a double quote. OMO's non-interactive-env hook detached every command containing the word git the same way; that half is OMO ledger fix 17-tool-args-in-place (oh-my-openagent-fix/local-fixes, 2026-10-02), which makes OMO edit the args in place. With it the Claude hook's rewrite would take effect too, but it only emits the POSIX form (wrong for a PowerShell shell) and also compresses Task prompts, so the exclusion stays and the shell-aware plugin is the only wrapper under OpenCode. Remove only with an owner decision on which wrapper should run.
